title: Born in Madisonville; drummer brother and Bunk Johnson inspire him
summary: Ernie was born in 1911 across Lake Pontchartrain. His musically inclined family included an older drummer brother who played with Bunk Johnson, and Ernie began on drums at about five.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I was born April 2nd, 1911 in Madisonville, Louisiana. On the other side of Punchetran Lake.

Can you tell us about your parents? Really just ask a few questions now and then. This doesn't have to be in any special order. We can jump back and forth in your life. It doesn't matter if it's all right straight into what you live. Can you tell us about your parents? Did they play any instrument?
Well, no, they didn't actually play an instrument, but they was musically inclined. How did you like to play that? My elder brother, he was a musician. He was a drummer.

No, he died in 1941. What was his name? Yeah, Cagnoletti. Cagnoletti. He played with Bung Johnson during World War I in Madisonville when they were launching ships. And that would give me my inspiration to play trumpet by here in Bung Johnson. That's the first trumpet player I've ever heard.
What did your brother play? He played drums.

What did you play? That started me playing music at the age of five. I started playing drums. In fact, he had two sets. And when he would leave Madison to go around Ibiza Spring, those places to play with Bung Johnson, he'd leave a set of drums at the Sons of Leobol in Madisonville where I think in those days it was showing silent pictures. He had a piano player while the pianola would play during the pitch and when the pitch was over, she would play the piano. Her name was Leona Bayham. She'd play the piano and I'd play the drums for her. And I was about five years old at that time.
